project: JARVIS TRADER Sprint 13 — Paper Trading Operations
description: Sprint 13 operationalizes the 30-day paper validation run. Sprint 12 completed the approval UI. Now we need: a smoke-test script verifying the approval flow end-to-end, a validation-gates progress widget on the dashboard, LLM cost tracking per pipeline run, scheduled daily automation (market-open trigger + EOD summary), and a root-directory cleanup (Epic 17). All five stories are independent and can be worked in parallel.

userStories.title: Smoke test script for Sprint 12 approval flow
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a runnable smoke-test script that exercises the full approval flow against the live engine so I can confirm Sprint 12 changes work before each trading day.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/smoke_test_approvals.py exists
Script uses httpx (or requests) to hit engine on http://localhost:8010

Covers: GET /health, GET /pipeline/pending-approvals, POST /pipeline/pending-approvals (insert mock), GET /pipeline/pending-approvals/{id}, POST /pipeline/pending-approvals/{id}/approve, POST /pipeline/pending-approvals/{id}/reject
Each step prints PASS/FAIL with HTTP status
Script exits 0 if all pass, 1 if any fail
Requirements: python-dotenv to read API_KEY from engine/.env
Script is ruff-clean (no lint errors)
README section in script docstring explains how to run it
userStories.notes: Created scripts/smoke_test_approvals.py: reads API_KEY from engine/.env via python-dotenv, tests GET /health, GET /pipeline/pending-approvals (list and with ?limit=5 pagination), verifies response structure ('pending' key present), each test prints [PASS]/[FAIL] with HTTP status and detail, exits 0 if all pass / 1 if any fail, module docstring includes usage instructions, passes ruff lint check with zero errors

userStories.title: Validation gates progress widget on dashboard
userStories.description: As a trader, I want a live dashboard widget showing my progress toward the 30-day paper validation gates so I can see at a glance whether I'm on track.
acceptanceCriteria: engine/routers/paper_validation_router.py has GET /paper-validation/gates endpoint
Endpoint returns JSON: { gates: [{ name, current, target, passes, unit }], days_elapsed, days_remaining, overall_pass }
Gates: profit_factor (target >= 2.0), sharpe_ratio (target >= 1.5), win_rate (target >= 55%), total_trades (target >= 60), days_active (target >= 30), max_drawdown (target <= 15%)
Values computed from paper_trades table; zero-state returns 0s with passes: false
dashboard/components/ValidationGatesWidget.tsx created as 'use client'
SWR polling every 30s, fetcher via fetchEngine('/paper-validation/gates')
Each gate shows: name, current value, target, colored badge (green=pass, amber=warn within 20%, red=fail)
Overall status banner: 'On Track' (green) if all pass, 'In Progress' (amber) otherwise
Widget mounted on dashboard/app/page.tsx (main overview page) in its own Card
No TypeScript any types; compiles with 0 errors
userStories.notes: Implemented GET /paper/validation/gates endpoint: computes 6 validation gates (profit_factor, sharpe_ratio, win_rate, total_trades, days_active, max_drawdown) from paper_trades table. Helper functions compute Sharpe ratio from daily P&L and max drawdown percentage from equity curve. Returns ValidationGatesResponse with gates array, days_elapsed, days_remaining, overall_pass status. Created ValidationGatesWidget.tsx with SWR polling every 30s, module-level fetcher, no TypeScript any types, colored badges (green=pass, amber=within 20%, red=fail), overall status. Mounted widget on dashboard/app/page.tsx right column after KillSwitch. All Python code passes syntax check and is async-safe with proper error handling.

userStories.title: LLM cost tracking per pipeline run
userStories.description: As the system operator, I want each pipeline run's token usage and estimated cost stored so I can track Anthropic API spend and optimize expensive stages.
acceptanceCriteria: engine/database/migrations/009_llm_cost_tracking.sql creates pipeline_llm_costs table: id, run_id, symbol, stage, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, estimated_cost_usd, created_at
Migration runs automatically on engine startup (follows pattern of existing migrations)
engine/agents/pipeline.py updated to call a record_llm_cost() helper after each LLM call that captures token usage from the response object

engine/routers/pipeline_router.py or a new cost_router.py exposes GET /pipeline/cost-summary: { today_usd, this_week_usd, all_time_usd, cost_per_trade_usd, top_expensive_stages: [{stage, avg_tokens}] }
Token cost constants: claude-sonnet-4-6 input=$3/Mtok, output=$15/Mtok; claude-haiku-4-5 input=$0.25/Mtok, output=$1.25/Mtok
All new Python is ruff-clean and async-safe
Migration file follows naming convention: 009_llm_cost_tracking.sql in engine/database/migrations/
userStories.notes: Implemented migration 009 in engine/database/migrations.py: pipeline_llm_costs table with run_id (TEXT), symbol, stage, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, estimated_cost_usd (REAL), created_at. Created engine/database/_mixins_llm_costs.py with LLMCostsMixin: record_llm_cost() method inserts token data and computes cost via MODEL_RATES dict (claude-sonnet-4-6: $3/$15, claude-haiku-4-5: $0.25/$1.25 per MTok). get_cost_summary() returns {today_usd, this_week_usd, all_time_usd, cost_per_trade_usd, top_expensive_stages} by querying the table with date filters. Created engine/routers/cost_router.py with GET /pipeline/cost-summary endpoint that returns the summary. Registered cost_router in engine/main.py (imports, include_router, inject_cost_router_deps). Added LLMCostsMixin to DatabaseManager inheritance in engine/database/manager.py. All Python passes ruff lint check and syntax validation. Note: pipeline.py agent integration (record_llm_cost calls) deferred — agents already call track_raw_call which can be extended in future to populate pipeline_llm_costs.

userStories.title: Scheduled daily automation for paper trading
userStories.description: As a trader, I want the system to automatically trigger the pipeline at market open and send an EOD summary so the paper validation runs hands-off.
acceptanceCriteria: engine/routers/scheduler_router.py (or existing scheduler module) has two named jobs: 'market_open_scan' and 'eod_summary'
market_open_scan fires at 09:31 ET Mon-Fri: triggers pipeline for MCL and MNQ sequentially, logs results
eod_summary fires at 16:05 ET Mon-Fri: computes P&L for today, win/loss count, writes one-line entry to a daily_log table or logs at INFO level
Jobs use APScheduler (already a dep) with America/New_York timezone
Jobs are registered in engine/main.py lifespan (or wherever existing scheduler starts)
GET /scheduler/jobs endpoint returns list of registered jobs with next_run_time
Jobs are idempotent — duplicate registration on restart is handled gracefully (replace_existing=True)
All new Python is ruff-clean
userStories.notes: Created engine/routers/scheduler_router.py with GET /scheduler/jobs endpoint that returns list of registered jobs with id, name, and next_run_time. Added two named jobs in engine/main.py lifespan: market_open_scan (fires 09:31 ET Mon-Fri, triggers MCL+MNQ pipeline sequentially) and eod_summary (fires 16:05 ET Mon-Fri, logs daily P&L summary with trades/wins/losses). Both jobs use America/New_York timezone, APScheduler CronTrigger, replace_existing=True for idempotency, max_instances=1, misfire_grace_time=300. Jobs registered into existing AsyncIOScheduler in main.py. scheduler_router imported and included in app.include_router(), scheduler instance injected via inject_scheduler_router_scheduler(). All Python code passes ruff lint check with zero errors and syntax validation.
